src/application/order-service.ts placeOrder: calls Product.canReserve and Product.reserve for the rules, then saves through the repositories (orchestration)
src/application/order-service.ts advance/cancel: Order.advanceTo and Order.cancel handle state changes; the service coordinates the stock side effects across aggregates
src/application/order-service.ts: no HTTP, SQL, file system or framework code
src/application/order-service.ts placeOrder: line merging and quantity validation are borderline and could live in the Order domain model, but they are not a clear layer violation
parsedVerdict.reasoning: OrderService is an application service. It handles use cases: adding a product, placing, advancing and cancelling orders, and querying stock. It loads aggregates through injected repository ports and calls domain methods for the state rules (Product.canReserve/reserve/consumeReserved/release, Order.advanceTo/cancel). It then saves the results through the ports. Coordinating two aggregates is an application concern, for example consuming reserved stock when an order ships or releasing it on cancel. The same goes for validating every line before reserving any stock so a failed order reserves nothing. The input checks (required ids, positive integer quantities, known state filter) are request validation, which also fits this layer. The file has no persistence code, no HTTP or transport handling and no framework code. Generating the order id with randomUUID and taking the current time are reasonable to do here. Two things could arguably move into the Order domain model: merging duplicate lines and validating each line's quantity. They are minor and do not clearly break the layer's role. No ADR prose was given.
